site of the first courthouse cass county s first courthouse was a plain wooden building 34 by 24 feet ordered by the county board in 1835 for about 450 and built by joseph harper all three county histories put it on lot 4 block 2 north range 1 west of the village plat the west side of broadway in the second block north of state street it served until the second courthouse opened in 1841 nothing of it survives this stop marks that stretch of broadway the exact building line is not known

local history branch carnegie library built over the winter of 1908 09 with a 10 000 gift from andrew carnegie this was the town s public library for more than 80 years cassopolis was one of 53 michigan communities to receive carnegie library money from 1947 to 1957 its basement also housed the cass county library and after the 1993 merger that created the cass district library it reopened in october 1994 as the local history branch the cass district library s local history branch a genealogy and county history research library mon thu 9 4 restored in 2012 and renovated again in 2020 21

cass county historic courthouse the stone courthouse with its tall clock tower was designed by the grand rapids firm rush bowman rush and finished in 1900 by the contractors james rowson and august mohnke after the county dismissed its first builder in 1898 it cost 43 797 88 with furniture and heating and stands on the northeast quarter of the old public square where the 1841 courthouse stood for nearly sixty years the county jail of 1852 stood just north of it empty after the courts moved out in 2003 it was restored with federal arpa and usda money and reopened in october 2024 as county offices administrator clerk register of deeds treasurer and the board of commissioners

the fort the county office building built in 1860 this brick building held the county s offices the clerk the probate court the register of deeds and the treasurer until the stone courthouse across the way was finished in 1899 the supervisors ordered it built fireproof after a fire in the village had alarmed them about the county s records it was later a laundry and in 1923 the masons bought it for their temple and added the large hall at the back in 1925 by 1906 it was commonly called the fort no source we have read says why the state lists it on the michigan state register of historic sites 1985 as the cass county office building masonic temple for some years it has been the turtle lodge an event hall with offices and apartments it changed hands in 2022

the old public square broadway state the 1831 village plat set aside a public square of 26 by 20 rods for county buildings with broadway and state street crossing at its center in 1839 the county deeded most of it to the court house company which built the 1841 courthouse merchants then built on the other quarters among them asa kingsbury s brick stores of 1869 70 on the southwest quarter the county sued in 1879 to win the square back and lost in the michigan supreme court in 1880 which is why the old square is now a row of business blocks early taverns faced it too the union hotel on the west side of broadway and the eagle hotel on the east side a downtown crossroads of two state highways with streetscape improvements laid along broadway and east state in 2020

the old courthouse s second life the county s second courthouse was a two storey frame building with classical columns finished in 1841 for 6 000 when the stone courthouse replaced it it was sold at auction for 25 and moved to the south side of state street west of broadway where the 1906 county history found it in use as a storage house a theatre history says it later became the 420 seat colonial opera house then the colonial theatre in 1909 and in 1937 was remodelled as the gem theatre which showed films until about 1960 the building was torn down in 1968

the bank corner banking began on this side of the old square in 1855 when asa and charles kingsbury opened a private bank the brothers parted in 1857 in 1868 asa kingsbury divided the square s southwest quarter into six lots and by 1869 70 two storey brick stores stood there with his own brick banking house among them the first national bank of cassopolis was organised in november 1870 with kingsbury as president and around 1899 it bought 32 000 of the county s bonds to pay for the new courthouse the two storey brick building at 116 south broadway is a former bank with its vaults still inside whether it is the first national s own building has not been confirmed

united presbyterian church the congregation was founded in march 1842 as the first presbyterian church when cassopolis was still little more than a clearing in the woods its first church begun in 1845 was dedicated in november 1846 and the present brick church at state and o keefe streets was completed on 10 december 1893 in 1938 the congregation joined with the village s baptist church it long served as a federated church for several denominations before taking its present presbyterian name in 1968 still a presbyterian congregation half a block east of broadway

the old post office storefront local accounts though not the old county histories say this storefront was one of the village s post offices in the late 1800s a board inside is signed 1897 it later held a barbershop and a thrift shop and about 2011 a local dentist dr roger pecina fitted it out as a prohibition style room with a salvaged 38 foot bar steve and shelley schroeder bought it in 2018 and have run it since 2021 as holden green tavern its address is given as both 151 and 159 south broadway check before you go in

the sinclair station an old dx filling station that had stood empty for about thirty years was bought by dr roger pecina who spent three years restoring it as a 1952 style sinclair station with period pumps a vintage police car and a wrecker it opened free to visitors around 2011 although no sinclair station had ever stood here a 2019 report said the antiques had been sold and the building had become an auto detailing shop see it from the sidewalk

pioneer log cabin museum proposed by charles harmon of the cass county pioneer society the cabin was raised in a single day may 23 1923 by a crew of 46 men led by ed ferguson they used numbered logs donated from farms across the county each matched to its giver and tree species its doors are black walnut and its stair rail came from an 1845 barn it opened as a pioneer relic museum in june 1924 a volunteer run museum in a village park open at times through the season see the museum s website pioneerlogcabinmuseum com

dowagiac area history museum the town s history museum began at southwestern michigan college and moved downtown in 2013 taking over a building that had held retail shops its biggest story is the round oak stove company which philo d beckwith incorporated in 1871 after casting his first stove around 1867 to heat his own foundry the company stopped making stoves in 1946 and its buildings were sold in 1947 a free museum tuesday friday 10 5 saturday 10 2 with about 4 000 square feet of exhibits including what is described as the largest public collection of round oak heating stoves in the world
A stop on the Front Street walk

the heddon museum the museum tells the story of james heddon who in the late 1890s whittled a piece of wood while waiting by the mill pond saw a bass strike it when he tossed it in and went on to make a top water lure he named the dowagiac james heddon s sons ran from 1902 to 1984 and by the 1920s was the world s biggest maker of quality fishing tackle also turning out golf shafts ski poles violin bows box kites and in world war ii radio antennae a volunteer run museum of the dowagiac area history museum open tuesday and friday 10 5 call ahead with more than 1 000 lures 140 reels and 150 rods

the fair store block a store called the fair was here by 1899 when the city directory listed emanuel tobias as its owner the block then held a run of other businesses until 1941 when the fair came back as a large department store that kept its doors open into the 1970s present occupant not confirmed

beckwith park and the beckwith memorial theatre site open park ground from 1848 this corner became the site of the beckwith memorial in 1892 built in memory of round oak founder p d beckwith by his daughter and son in law in lake superior red sandstone and dedicated in january 1893 besides a 600 seat theatre counted among the finest between new york and chicago the building held a bank city hall and the round oak company offices films were shown from 1914 it was torn down in 1966 and a bank building later stood on part of the lot the city bought that in 2019 took it down in 2020 and added the ground to the park beckwith park renovated and reopened in july 2021 a piece of the theatre s red sandstone wall still shows on the building next door

caruso s candy soda shop the building that went up after an 1864 fire held a grocery a barber shop a department store and in 1908 09 the state savings bank in 1910 the chicago candy kitchen opened here making candy and ice cream and adding a soda fountain in 1914 antonio anthony caruso and his wife emilia took over the business in september 1922 still run by the caruso family now in its third generation making chocolates and caramels and serving sundaes and lunch at the soda fountain

front and commercial the brick downtown fires in the 1860s destroyed most of the first wooden stores on front and commercial streets and brick blocks took their place mostly between the late 1860s and the 1880s a 1910 newspaper item quoted in the museum booklet reported that the state savings bank would move from 130 s front to this corner the heart of the downtown commercial district revitalized in the 1990s when m 51 was rerouted and depot drive was laid out

1913 elks temple wounded minnow saloon raised in 1913 as a three story downtown temple it had shops at street level and club rooms a pool hall and a small theatre above over the decades the ground floor held grocery stores a state liquor store and taverns the wounded minnow saloon fills the ground floor and a 2025 plan adds apartments upstairs as part of a 9 million state grant for downtown

moore grocery building george moore built this as a grocery and meat market around 1900 and had retired by 1908 merwin and bonnell traded here into the 1920s and by 1938 w f lyon and son ran a funeral undertaking and furniture business in it followed by a string of other shops present occupant not confirmed

michigan central railroad depot the michigan central built this brick tudor revival station for about 13 000 in 1902 03 replacing an earlier wooden depot it is credited to the architects spier and rohns who also designed the niles station it went on the national register in 1993 and in 1995 the city restored it as part of the 1 8 million depot drive project keeping the original floor mosaic with the railroad s initials a working amtrak stop blue water and wolverine owned by the city with the greater dowagiac chamber of commerce and a gift shop inside

judd lumber company mark judd put up a sawmill here in 1859 and he and william judd added a lumber yard in 1889 the sawmill ran into the 1950s and the judd family kept the business until 2019 still a working lumber yard now run as us lumber company and billed as michigan s oldest

commercial and pennsylvania where the first round oak stove stood a small early business district grew up at this corner and its first buildings burned in a fire in the 1860s beckwith s very first stove heated his own foundry but the first round oak stove offered for sale was set up in a barber shop here where the townsmen would see it and it stayed there until 1895 the exact lot is not known the stop marks the corner present buildings and occupants not confirmed

dowagiac district library carnegie library dowagiac won a 12 500 carnegie grant in january 1903 and the library dates its founding to 1904 in 2004 it became a district library serving the city and the townships of silver creek keeler wayne and bainbridge the working public library with a genealogy and local history service

beckwith theatre company former methodist church this was the site of the town s first church open to all denominations in 1854 the children from the first orphan train were placed with local families here the methodists built a church on the spot in 1859 faced it in brick and took off its steeple in a 1906 remodeling and worshipped here until 1974 home of the beckwith theatre company a volunteer community theatre named for the lost beckwith memorial theatre its first season in 1990 was staged on the third floor of the elks temple on front street the city s website dates the building to 1925 but a museum photograph of about 1865 shows this same church so its core is the 1859 church as refaced in 1906

round oak stove company philo d beckwith philo d beckwith opened a foundry in dowagiac in the 1850s and cast his first stove around 1867 to heat the struggling shop the michigan central railroad then ordered heaters for its depots between detroit and chicago and by 1871 stoves were his main product by 1900 round oak was one of the largest stove factories in the united states its 1890s advertising claimed more than a million round oak stoves were in use
Dowagiac Drill Company / Dowagiac Manufacturing Co. (grain drills)

dowagiac drill company dowagiac manufacturing co grain drills grew out of p d beckwith s grain drill trade before stoves beckwith s dowagiac foundry was built around a roller grain drill an 1863 patented beckwith design used heavy cast iron wheels to smooth the soil as it planted and in 1869 michigan awarded him a silver medallion for his two horse drill the dowagiac drill company followed in 1881 dowagiac drills were sold across the united states and in europe south america and asia and 1899 advertising called the works the largest drill factory in existence

james heddon s sons james heddon with his sons the story goes that james heddon a former beekeeper was whittling by dowagiac s mill pond in the late 1890s when a bass struck a piece of wood he tossed into the water he went on to build a top water lure he called the dowagiac the company was founded in 1902 first making lures by hand in the family kitchen and in a new dowagiac factory by 1904 by the 1920s it was called the world s largest producer of quality fishing tackle most of its workers were women

kawneer company francis j plym architect francis j plym a swedish born architect patented a way of framing plate glass shop windows in heavy rolled copper which would neither rot like wood nor rust like iron the patent was granted may 15 1906 the company name came from kansas city s kaw river local promoter carmi r smith is said to have met plym while he was changing trains at niles and in early 1907 the company moved there with help from the local business men s association kawneer grew from window frames to door frames and complete shop fronts

clark equipment company eugene b clark with george r rich s drill company the company began in chicago making a tougher drill for boring holes in steel rails and moved to buchanan in 1904 when the chamber of commerce offered free rent and cheap power eugene b clark a 33 year old illinois steel engineer took over management and the firm became celfor tool 1906 and then clark equipment 1916 buchanan made steel truck wheels and an internal gear drive axle that became an industry standard foundry workers built a gas powered shop buggy to move material around the plant as the trucktractor it was sold to others and its features went into clark s lift truck in 1927

sheffield car company sheffield velocipede car co george s sheffield with warren willits and e b linsley george s sheffield a michigan farmer patented a three wheeled railroad hand car patent no 213 254 11 march 1879 and built the business in three rivers in 1888 charles h morse of fairbanks morse co bought willits s interest and fairbanks morse became the sales agent for sheffield products the company was reorganized as sheffield car co in 1892 by 1896 it offered velocipedes with small gasoline engines and one estimate puts velocipede output at about 4 000 a sheffield velocipede survives at the buckinghamshire railway centre in england

studebaker henry and clement studebaker h c studebaker henry and clement studebaker opened a blacksmith shop in south bend on 16 february 1852 with 68 in capital and built two wagons in their first year the firm supplied wagons to the u s army made 6 000 vehicles in 1867 and over 75 000 by 1885 and became one of the world s largest makers of horse drawn vehicles it built an electric car in 1902 and a gasoline car in 1904 and made its last wagons in 1920

oliver chilled plow works south bend iron works james oliver james oliver a scottish immigrant received the first of 45 plow patents on june 30 1857 he chilled molten iron so a plow bottom had a glass hard face that polished like steel and scoured clean in sticky prairie soil the south bend iron works had 100 workers in 1868 in 1874 oliver bought 32 acres of farmland for a new factory daily shipments sometimes reached 30 to 40 railcars each carrying 150 to 200 plows and by 1901 the firm was called the world s largest plow maker styling itself plowmakers to the world
Made in the Valley · South Bend

singer manufacturing company cabinet works the singer manufacturing company singer set up its south bend cabinet works in 1868 on the east race and moved around 1900 to a larger site on division street now western avenue the plant made the wooden cabinets and cast iron stands and treadles for singer sewing machines it covered about 60 acres including 20 acres of lumber yards and about five miles of railroad track inside the factory

bendix corporation bendix aviation vincent bendix vincent bendix of moline illinois invented the starter drive that made the automobile self starter practical in 1924 he founded the bendix corporation in south bend to make automobile brake systems it became bendix aviation in 1929 and made automotive aviation marine radio and radar equipment he or his company held more than 5 500 patents bendix also founded the bendix transcontinental air race in 1931

mishawaka woolen manufacturing co ball band jacob beiger and martin v beiger owners from 1867 martin v beiger and adolphus eberhart invented an all knit boot in 1886 a red ball was added to the boots black band in 1891 and ball band was registered as a trademark in 1901 the first ball band rubber shoes were made in february 1898 the company motto was good enough will do ball band must be the best in 1951 it launched the red ball jets sports shoe

c g conn charles gerard conn charles g conn was making a rubber rimmed cornet mouthpiece by 1874 patented it in 1875 and began making instruments that year his first cornet designed with the french maker eugene dupont the mouthpiece idea the story goes came after he split his lip in a saloon fight by 1905 conn claimed the world s largest musical instrument factory and other makers followed him to elkhart by the 1970s about 40 of the world s band instruments were made in elkhart the band industry capital of the world
Dr. Miles Medical Company / Miles Laboratories

dr miles medical company miles laboratories dr franklin l miles dr franklin l miles moved his practice from chicago to elkhart in 1875 and in 1885 began the dr miles medical company to sell dr miles nervine and restorative nerve and liver pills the firm published dr miles new u s weather almanac from 1902 and won a place in law books with a 1911 u s supreme court price fixing case its best known product alka seltzer was first used on december 20 1930 and trademarked june 9 1931

gibson mandolin guitar manufacturing company orville gibson with five kalamazoo backers orville gibson a new yorker who came to kalamazoo in the 1880s worked as a clerk and carved mandolins in his spare time he was making them full time by 1896 and five local men then offered to fund a factory for his instruments the company moved to parsons street in 1917 and stayed nearly seven decades growing to about 120 000 square feet over a whole city block the super 400 1934 and the les paul 1952 were made there

kalamazoo celery growing george taylor cornelius de bruin and other dutch growers a scotsman george taylor is credited with planting celery in kalamazoo in 1856 cornelius de bruin who came from the netherlands in 1866 developed the stalk type and dutch farmers turned the muck lands into celery fields celery was shipped by rail from 1871 and vendors often young boys sold stalks to passengers at the michigan central depot growers wore wooden shoes and their horses wore wide wooden shoes to keep from sinking in the muck

the upjohn company dr william e upjohn with his brothers henry and james dr w e upjohn patented a friable pill in 1885 one that crumbled easily to powder when most hard pills passed through the body undissolved to prove it he mailed pine boards to thousands of physicians with his pills and rivals inviting them to hammer each pill into the wood and compare a thumb crushing a pill became the company trademark for about 60 years in the 1950s upjohn s chemistry made steroids such as cortisone affordable and later products included motrin and rogaine

checker cab manufacturing checker motors morris markin morris markin a russian born tailor who had taken over a chicago cab fleet formed the checker cab manufacturing corporation in may 1922 and moved production to two empty auto plants on pitcher street in kalamazoo in 1923 albert kahn designed new buildings in 1929 by 1965 more than a quarter of the nation s cabs were checkers and they became a new york city icon detroit automakers refused filming access for the 1978 film blue collar so it was shot at the checker plant

shakespeare company william shakespeare jr william shakespeare jr patented a level winding fishing reel in 1896 which laid line evenly on the spool so anglers no longer had to guide it with a thumb and founded his company in kalamazoo in 1897 the firm grew from water street to pitcher street 1913 and to 241 e kalamazoo ave 1939 from 1945 it made the first fiberglass fishing rods a 1948 strike of about 700 workers led to a riot and a record length conspiracy trial

kalamazoo stove company the kalamazoo stove company made stoves and furnaces from 1902 to 1952 and was one of the first manufacturers to sell directly to customers by mail rather than through stores under the slogan a kalamazoo direct to you in 1937 its peak year it made 100 000 stoves
